title: Diminutives and Augmentatives
summary: Use -inho, -zinho, -ão, and related forms for size, affection, irony, and emphasis.

sections.heading: Diminutives beyond size
sections.body: Diminutives like **-inho/-inha** and **-zinho/-zinha** can mean small, cute, affectionate, modest, polite, or ironic depending on context and intonation.

sections.heading: Choosing -inho or -zinho
sections.body: Many words take **-inho** directly; others use **-zinho** to preserve shape or sound. Gender and plural still matter.

sections.heading: Augmentatives and evaluation
sections.body: Augmentatives like **-ão/-ona** can indicate large size, admiration, intensity, or sometimes criticism. Meanings are lexicalized in some words.

examples.en: She is a very caring mother.

keyPoints: Diminutives express attitude, not only small size.
Cafezinho is culturally common and often hospitable.
Augmentatives can be positive or negative.
Tone and context determine affection, irony, or criticism.

commonMistakes.right: Diminutive can express affection, politeness, irony, or intensity.
